newsitem.title: GERMANY: Iran debt to Germany plays role in ties -ministry.
newsitem.headline: Iran debt to Germany plays role in ties -ministry.

text.p: Iran's debt to Germany of 13 billion marks ($8.65 billion) is one factor behind Bonn's efforts to maintain diplomatic relations with Tehran, the Foreign Ministry said on Monday.
A spokesman confirmed a report in Handelsblatt newspaper quoting Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel as saying economic motives were a factor driving Bonn's policies towards Iran.
"Naturally economic aspects play a role, but it is only a minor role," the spokesman said.
Annual debt servicing payments of one billion marks could be in jeopardy if Bonn severed diplomatic ties with Tehran, as some politicians in Germany have urged, the newspaper said.
Relations between Germany and Iran have been strained since German prosecutors demanded life sentences for an Iranian and a Lebanese on trial in Germany for the killing of three Kurdish dissidents.
Accusations by the prosecutors that Tehran had ordered the murders provoked outrage in Iran.

German exports to Iran have fallen to 2.3 billion marks in 1995 from 9.1 billion marks in 1992 while imports from Iran have been stagnant at 1.1 billion marks. Iran ranks 42nd on the list of leading export markets for Germany.
